description: Design tokens for the four apps. The Smile ID design system is the single source; this file records where it lives, how each platform consumes it, and the deltas found when the design file was checked against it on 2026-08-12.

source.name: smile-design-system
source.shape: three-tier DTCG JSON — primitive → semantic → component — with pre-generated per-platform outputs
source.rule: Reference the highest tier that fits: component tokens when building that named component, semantic tokens otherwise. Never reference a primitive from app code, and never hardcode a hex.
source.why: The SDK's theme and these apps resolve from the same generated source, so the sample matches the SDK's branding without importing SDK components or copying values.

verification.method: Figma variable definitions on the products board (node 5206-4037) compared against the design system's resolved light values.
verification.result: Aligned. Every colour, the radius scale and the type family match exactly. The badge treatment was later resolved against the prototype recording — see the softBadgeFills delta.

later.method: get_variable_defs resolves a frame in its OWN mode, so the light frame returns the light column and the dark frame the dark one; get_design_context's var(--token, fallback) carries the default-mode value as a cross-check. Both were run on both frames.
later.result: The five variables below match the vendored tokens exactly in both modes. Two gaps have no token at all and are recorded as the offBlack and floatingElevation deltas. Which variable PAINTS which surface is not recorded here — see docs/plan/products-visual-refresh-android.md §3.4, where the two frames bind Main BG and Card BG opposite to their names.

matches.token: color.surface (light) — mode-invariant in the design, and the session card's text colour

deltas.severity: blocks StatusBadge on all four statuses
deltas.fillsSource: Read off the four JobRow badge instances on the Verifications board 2026-08-17 (nodes 5206:2429, 2430, 2432, 2433), where each pair is bound to a design variable — color/ok-bg + color/ok-fg, color/info-*, color/warn-*, color/err-*. These are the values the earlier prototype recording could only describe as 'pale'.
deltas.labelCase: Title case, not UPPERCASE. The design sets 'Clear' / 'Processing' / 'Attention' / 'Blocked' at 11/700 with 0.88 tracking — the Label type style at label size, but not upper-cased. Date and section headers DO upper-case the same style, which is why the app upper-cased this one too.
deltas.finding: CONFIRMED from the prototype recording 2026-08-12: the design uses SOFT tinted pills for ALL FOUR statuses (pale green Clear, pale amber Attention, pale red Blocked, pale blue Processing). The design system's badge.* tokens are saturated fills with inverse text, so no current token pair produces the intended treatment.
deltas.recommendation: Add soft badge variants to the design system (background + text per role). This is now a system gap rather than a per-status judgement call: the design applies soft fills consistently, and hardcoding the Figma hexes would bypass the token source.
deltas.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: keep the design's soft treatment and ADD soft badge variants to the design system (background + text per role for success/warning/error/info). Do not hardcode locally; the existing saturated pairs stay for surfaces that want them. INTERIM 2026-08-17: review found the badges still shipping saturated, because 'do not hardcode locally' left them with no source at all. `fills` above is now generated into each platform exactly as productHues is — one source in spec/, no hex in component code — so all four apps agree while the design system catches up. Delete the generated file, not the delta, once the design system carries the soft roles.

deltas.severity: dark-mode defect in the token source
deltas.finding: color.border does not change between light and dark. A #EAECF0 border on the dark background (#1A1C23) is near-maximum contrast and will read as a bright outline around every card and row. CONFIRMED ON A DEVICE 2026-08-13, the first time anything rendered these tokens in dark mode: the Android shell's nav-bar pill draws a bright near-white outline on #1A1C23, exactly as predicted. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-13 across the U1 primitives: every TextInput, SearchField and Toast outline, and every off/disabled Switch track, draws bright white on dark.
deltas.rootCause: semantic/dark/color.json DOES define border — it points at the same {color.grey.200} as light, and its own $description says 'SDK keeps stroke light at low opacity on dark; consumers may apply ~15% opacity'. So the intent is a translucent stroke, but the instruction is delegated to consumers: the generated per-platform output emits a fully opaque #EAECF0 and carries no opacity, and this repo's own rule forbids app-side colour arithmetic, so a consumer cannot legitimately apply it. The same is true of color.text.muted (see darkMuted).
deltas.propagation: 12 tokens resolve through color.border and so inherit the defect — border, banner.border, card.border, filter.trigger-border, filter.popover-border, filter.chip-border, input.border, search.border, skeleton.highlight, table.border, table.row-border, tab.border — and 11 more through color.text.muted. They reference the semantic role correctly, so fixing the two semantic tokens fixes all 23. That makes this a high-leverage one-line fix, not 23 fixes.
deltas.recommendation: Resolve the dark value to the translucent colour the $description describes (e.g. rgba(234,236,240,0.15)) rather than delegating opacity to consumers — the generators already emit rgba() correctly. Do not patch it locally.
deltas.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: fix in the design system, not locally. Suggested values: color.border dark → a subtle dark-grey (e.g. #333846); color.text.muted dark → a lighter grey clearing 4.5:1 (e.g. #9BA1AC). Raise before U0 wires dark mode.

deltas.severity: worth checking
deltas.finding: Muted text is the same grey in both modes. On the dark background that lands near the 4.5:1 threshold for small text, and muted text is used for supporting lines and the date group headers.
deltas.recommendation: Ask for a lighter muted grey in dark mode, or verify the contrast ratio and accept it explicitly.
deltas.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: fix in the design system, not locally. Suggested values: color.border dark → a subtle dark-grey (e.g. #333846); color.text.muted dark → a lighter grey clearing 4.5:1 (e.g. #9BA1AC). Raise before U0 wires dark mode.

deltas.severity: cosmetic
deltas.finding: Fully-rounded in Figma versus a fixed 32 in the generated output. Identical on a 48-tall button (anything ≥ 24 renders as a pill) but different on taller surfaces.
deltas.recommendation: No action for buttons. If a taller pill appears, treat 999 as the intent.

deltas.severity: emitter asymmetry — blocked U1 typography
deltas.finding: The Compose emitter writes all 29 type styles as COMMENTS, so MaterialTheme.typography is stock unless the app maps them itself. The Dart emitter produces 29 real TextStyles from the same resolved tokens.flat.json, and the SwiftUI emitter omits type entirely. This is an emitter asymmetry, not a platform limit: a Compose TextStyle needs no FontFamily to exist, and the emitter already holds every field it would need — build.mjs emitCompose() formats fontSize/fontWeight/lineHeight into a comment string and DROPS fontFamily and letterSpacing while doing it, so the comment is lossy as well as unusable.
deltas.recommendation: Ask upstream to make the Compose emitter emit real TextStyles, parameterised on font families the app supplies (the shape this repo generates is a working proposal). Until then scripts/sync_design_tokens.py generates them here, which keeps them generated rather than hand-copied and lets --check fail on staleness. Delete the generated file when upstream lands.
deltas.status: STOPGAP IN THIS REPO 2026-08-13 — android/sample-ui/.../tokens/SmileTypeStyles.kt is generated from the same source and mirrors the Dart emitter's names so the two stay diffable.

deltas.severity: affects every component's metrics
deltas.finding: emitCompose() and emitSwift() both filter dimensions to the top-level groups {spacing, radius, size, space, border-width}, so every COMPONENT dimension is dropped: button.height (52), button.padding-x/y, input.height (44), input.radius, search.height/gap, badge.radius/padding-x/padding-y, avatar.radius/size-sm/md/lg, card.radius/padding/gap. components.json names several of these as the tokens a primitive must use, and none of them exist in the Compose output.
deltas.recommendation: Ask upstream to emit component dimensions alongside component colours. Meanwhile the primitives reference the semantic scale token that carries the identical value (button.height → size.control-lg 52, input/search.height → size.control-md 44, input/search.radius → radius.field 12, button.radius → radius.control 32, badge.radius → radius.chip 999, avatar.radius → radius.full 999). avatar.size-md (40) has NO scale equivalent and falls back to space.40.
deltas.note: components.json describes Button as 48dp tall; the token source says button.height = 52px. The design system wins per the rules in this file, so the primitives use 52.

deltas.severity: dark-mode defect in the token source
deltas.finding: tokens/component/button.json references the primitive {color.grey.200} for the disabled background instead of a semantic role, so it cannot re-resolve per mode — contradicting that file's own _comment, which states component tokens 'reference SEMANTIC roles only, so they re-resolve per light/dark automatically'. CONFIRMED ON A DEVICE 2026-08-13: the disabled Button draws a near-white #EAECF0 slab on the dark background. Distinct from darkBorder, and NOT fixed by fixing color.border.
deltas.recommendation: Point button.disabled.background at a semantic role that has a dark value. Do not patch locally.

deltas.severity: blocks ProductCard on every product; the two document products are told apart by hue alone
deltas.source: Re-read node by node off BOTH frames 2026-08-25 — light 5487:1351 and dark 5447:1701, which carry byte-identical gradients. Endpoints from get_design_context's linear-gradient; icon tints from the exported glyph SVGs, which is the only place they are readable (get_variable_defs does not expose them).
deltas.shape: from/to are the gradient endpoints and fromAlpha/toAlpha the alpha each stop carries — kept beside the colour rather than baked into it, because kotlin_color applies alpha at the use site by design. stopStart/stopEnd are the stop positions as fractions and MAY EXCEED 1: the design runs the outer stop past the card's edge. angle is the CSS gradient angle, recorded for the ports and not consumed on Android. cardIcon tints the card's glyph; icon and tile are the list row's pair, which the products frame does not govern.

Both its hue and its icon are derived here so the grid is complete, and both are placeholders a designer should confirm or replace. Until then this entry is the source and scripts/sync_design_tokens.py generates SmileProductHues.kt from it — the same stopgap shape as composeTypeStylesAreComments. deltas.iconTintsChanged: The card's tint moved on three of the six and none of them follows the gradient: documentVerification -> #06A850, enhancedDocumentVerification -> #04713A, enhancedKyc -> #0EA5E9. smartSelfieEnrollment KEEPS its green #05723A although its card is now amber, which is why 'cardIcon = from' is not the rule.
deltas.scrimIsNotPerHue: REMOVED 2026-08-25. `scrim` was per-product and fed two different marks; both frames draw them uniform across all six cards, in two DIFFERENT colours: the go pill is rgba(45,43,42,0.16) — Off_black's light value at 16% — and the ghost glyph is WHITE at 10%. A per-hue field cannot express one value shared by six products, and the app had five white go pills where the design draws six dark ones. The card now takes the go pill from the offBlack token pinned light, and the ghost from the same colour-inverse ink its label already uses.
deltas.rowPairVsCard: RE-READ 2026-08-26 off the Verifications board, node 5206-2410 (spec/screens.json → verifications → states → default); glyph tints taken from the exported row SVGs' stroke, since no variable carries them. The row pair is NOT stale: all five tiles the board draws are identical to the values here and four of the five glyph tints are too. One moved — documentVerification's row glyph is #B36500, corrected above from #C46F00, which also lifts it from 3.26:1 to 3.84:1 on its pale amber tile. enhancedKyc has no row on this board, which predates the sixth product, so its icon/tile stay derived. What is left is a DESIGN question rather than a merge: the board draws Document Verification amber and Enhanced Document Verification near-black in the row while 5487:1351 draws their cards green and dark green, so one product is two colours on two surfaces by the two boards' own account. Escalated to additions.candidates rather than settled here — taking either side in code invents a value neither board carries.
deltas.stopsRunPastTheEdge: Four cards stop at 129.78% and biometricKyc at 110.51%, so the end colour is never fully reached on screen. Compose colour stops must land inside 0..1, so the card interpolates the colour the gradient has actually arrived at by the edge and uses THAT as its last stop — exact, and no custom shader. Clamping to 1.0 instead would over-saturate every card's far corner.

deltas.finding: spec/components.json references elevation.floating in five places and nothing defines it. The design's value is a CSS offset/blur/colour triple, which Compose cannot express: Modifier.shadow takes an elevation and derives offset and blur from the platform light model, and its ambientColor/spotColor tint the two shadow passes rather than setting the drawn rgba — and both are ignored below API 28. So the 8dp the app already ships matches the frame's 8px y-offset, and the blur and alpha are not reproducible without abandoning the token for two magic colours.
deltas.recommendation: Add a floating elevation role to the design system as a per-platform value — a dp elevation for Compose, the offset/blur/colour triple for CSS and SwiftUI — rather than one shape that only one platform can consume. Until then the nav bar keeps shadowElevation and this entry is where the design's value lives, so the number is recorded rather than pasted.

figma.note: The design draws no stroke at all on the verifications or settings lists, so those two were implemented from border-width.hairline and color.border by default rather than by drawing.

designSystem.colour: color.border and card.border are the SAME near-white #EAECF0 in BOTH modes — the generated light and dark outputs carry identical values, so there is no dark pair at all
designSystem.width: border-width.hairline is 1dp; there is no 0.5 step, and no fractional border-width token of any kind

deltas.finding: A mode-invariant near-white outline is not one treatment, it is two. Against the card surface #EAECF0 is 1.18:1 in light — the intended near-invisible hairline — and 12.09:1 in dark, where the same value becomes the loudest edge on the screen. That 10.90 spread is the defect, and it is why the dark verifications and settings lists read as outlined boxes while their light twins read as plain cards. #797C85 is 4.17:1 light and 3.43:1 dark, a 0.74 spread: one value that reads the same in both schemes, which is what a single mode-invariant token has to be to be correct. The 0.5 width halves the weight the higher contrast adds in light.
deltas.recommendation: Give color.border a real light/dark PAIR upstream, or add a subtle-outline role with one mid value that works in both. Also add a 0.5 border-width step: the design already draws 0.2 and 0.5 and the scale starts at 1. Generated from here meanwhile, exactly as offBlack and borderStrong are, so no component carries a hex or a raw dp.
deltas.status: OWNER RULING 2026-08-26 — one stroke everywhere: #797C85 at 0.5dp. This SUPERSEDES the 0.2 the products frame draws (recorded in cardLabelRuns) and the 1dp hairline the two lists inherited; uniform and subtle beat per-surface fidelity, because the frame never drew the lists at all.
deltas.guardedBy: UseSmileIDSampleContrastTest holds the stroke to a MAXIMUM as well as a minimum in both schemes — the only ceiling in that test, because here too much contrast was the defect.

deltas.severity: the products screen's card labels and the session card's text, on all four apps

figma.ink: white on every product card and on the session card

deltas.finding: White ink on the new fills clears WCAG AA on only 14 of the 28 gradient stops (6 cards x 2 stops x 2 schemes, plus the session card's 2 stops x 2). The worst is the Registration card's opaque amber #FFB53D at 1.76:1 — fully opaque, so it fails identically in BOTH schemes and is not a compositing artefact. On that fill dark ink would be markedly better than white, so the card is not merely below the bar, it is using the wrong end of the ramp. Next worst: #A78BFA at 0.79 over the light page (2.18:1, the session card AND Registration's outer stop), #0EA5E9 at 0.79 (2.28:1), #00AA99 at 0.79 (2.37:1) and #2CC05C (2.39:1).
deltas.recommendation: Design question, not a local nudge: either darken the light fills or give the card an ink that varies with its hue. Not fixed here because the owner ruled the frame final as drawn on 2026-08-24, and inventing a per-card ink would put four platforms on four different answers.
deltas.guardedBy: UseSmileIDSampleContrastTest holds these surfaces to DESIGN_INK_FLOOR (1.75), the design's own worst case, so a REGRESSION fails while today's values pass. It is a floor, not a certification — raise it as design raises the values. The same test now covers gradient-backed surfaces at all, which is how the session card shipped near-black ink on its own fill in dark mode for as long as dark mode has existed: no token pair described it.
deltas.status: OPEN 2026-08-26 — white ink ruled and shipped; the fill change is the outstanding design ask
deltas.resolution: OWNER RULING 2026-08-26, after seeing it on a device: the label and the go arrow stay WHITE on all six cards. Consistency across the grid beats per-card contrast, and the frame's uniform white-on-saturated is the most deliberate thing about the design. A luminance-picked label was built and rejected — it cleared AA everywhere (worst 5.90:1) but darkened three of the six cards, which read as inconsistent.
deltas.sessionCardResidual: The session card keeps white ink. Its gradient runs dark blue to light violet and the text spans both, so a single ink cannot serve both ends: the luminance rule would fix the countdown on the right and break the two runs on the left. Its right-hand stop is 2.18:1 over the light page — the same ask to design as the residual above, and the same fix (darken the stop).
deltas.whatStillAdapts: Only the two marks the design draws at a fixed value and which disappear at one end of the range: the go pill's scrim and the ghost glyph. One fixed value leaves the pill invisible on the darkest card and the ghost invisible on the lightest, both reported from the device. Neither is text.
deltas.theAskToDesign: Darken the four light `from` stops, or drop their alpha. That is the only fix that keeps white ink AND clears AA, because it moves the fill rather than the ink. Worst today is the amber Registration card at 1.76:1, then #A78BFA at 2.18:1, #0EA5E9 at 2.28:1, #00AA99 at 2.37:1 and #2CC05C at 2.39:1.

deltas.severity: the products header and both section headers, on all four apps

designSystem.text-style.heading-section: 18 / 24 at weight 600 — three points large and a weight light
designSystem.text-style.caption: 12 / 16 at weight 500 — MATCHES Type/Caption; the page subtitle was on body-sm (14/20/400) instead

The units trap matters here: Type/Heading reports letterSpacing -1, but that is -1% of 26px and the node renders -0.26px — implementing -1.sp is four times too tight.

deltas.severity: the floating nav bar on every screen of all four apps

figma.tabs pill: Main BG — #F9FAFB light, #1A1C23 dark (nodes I5487:1357;6:5 and I5447:1707;6:5)

designSystem.semantic: absent — there is no nav-bar role; the app used color.surface, which is LIGHTER than the page in dark

deltas.finding: The design recesses the pill BELOW the page: page Card BG, pill Main BG. This app cannot take that pairing, because its page is color.background and moving it to color.surface would repaint Verifications and Settings, whose rows ARE color.surface and would disappear into it. Taking only the pill half puts #1A1C23 on a #1A1C23 page, which is the invisible bar the plan predicted — verified on the re-recorded dark golden. So the bar needs its own fill: one step darker than the page in dark (#21232C, contrast 1.09:1 plus its shadow) and one step lighter in light (#FFFFFF on #F9FAFB), which is the design's relationship at the lightness this app's page allows.
deltas.recommendation: Ask design for a nav-bar role, or for the products page fill to be reconciled with the other two tabs. Generated from here meanwhile, exactly as borderStrong is, so no component references color.grey.800.
deltas.guardedBy: UseSmileIDSampleContrastTest asserts the pill stays distinguishable from the page in BOTH schemes.

android.consume: SmileTokens.kt — SmileColorLight / SmileColorDark / SmileDimens (SmileType is comments only); plus the generated SmileTypeStyles.kt for the type ramp
android.wiring: Feed the token objects into the app's Compose theme and select by isSystemInDarkTheme(); do not replace the SDK's own theme, which resolves the same tokens internally. Component tokens are grouped into the app's own mode-selected holder because SmileColorLight and SmileColorDark are two unrelated generated objects with no common supertype, so a component cannot choose between them itself.
android.generatedHere: android/sample-ui/.../tokens/SmileTypeStyles.kt — 29 real TextStyles, and the five DM Sans OFL faces in sample-ui/src/main/res/font/. Both come from scripts/sync_design_tokens.py --all and are covered by --check. The font is bundled rather than fetched through a downloadable-font provider: this file's rules say to ship it, and a provider would make text depend on Play Services and goldens depend on the network.

ios.wiring: Select by colorScheme and expose through the app's environment.

expo.wiring: A typed token module the sample-ui package imports; no native code involved.

flutter.generatedBy: scripts/sync_design_tokens.py, from the design system's platform-neutral dist/json/tokens.flat.json
flutter.wiring: Feed SmileColorLight / SmileColorDark into the app's ThemeData, selected by platform brightness.
flutter.shape: SmileColorLight (152) · SmileColorDark (152) · SmileDimens (42) · SmileType (29 TextStyles) · SmileShadows (6 BoxShadows) · SmileMotion (6 Durations)
flutter.deliberateAdditions: The upstream Compose emitter leaves typography as comments and omits shadows entirely. Dart expresses both directly, so SmileType emits real TextStyles and SmileShadows emits real BoxShadows. Naming otherwise mirrors Compose so the two are diffable. NOTE 2026-08-13: the typography half is an emitter gap rather than a Compose limitation — see deltas → composeTypeStylesAreComments. The shadow half is a genuine platform difference: Compose has no equivalent of an arbitrary offset/blur/colour shadow value.
flutter.verified: dart format canonical, generator idempotent, `dart analyze` clean in a Flutter package context, and colour membership identical to the Compose output.

rules: Tokens are generated, never hand-copied. A hex in app code is a review failure.
Light and dark both come from the token source; no app-side colour arithmetic.
Where the design file and the design system disagree, the design system wins and the disagreement is recorded in `deltas` above until the design team rules.
Fonts: DM Sans for UI, the display family for headlines. Ship DM Sans with the apps rather than relying on a system fallback.

additions.comment: Requests to the design system, not local overrides. Empty is the goal. Every entry below is a value the products and verifications work needed and the token source does not carry, so it ships as a generated stopgap recorded in `deltas` — and every one of them is a value the iOS, Flutter and React Native ports will each vendor separately until design resolves it. `deltas` stays the implementation record; this is the ask.
additions.readAgainst: Products, light 5487:1351 and dark 5447:1701, read 2026-08-25/26. Verifications, node 5206-2410, read 2026-08-26. File CT3oeBfk8uuyvRmGkRJ71D.

candidates.priority: P1 — accessibility, and the only entry here that is a defect rather than a naming gap
candidates.need: Darken the four light `from` stops, or drop their alpha. That is the only fix that keeps white ink AND clears WCAG AA, because it moves the fill rather than the ink.
candidates.why: The card label and its go arrow are WHITE on all six cards by owner ruling 2026-08-26, taken after seeing the alternative on a device: a luminance-picked label cleared AA everywhere at worst 5.90:1 and was rejected because it darkened three of the six cards and read as inconsistent. So the ink is settled and the fill is the only remaining variable. A per-card ink is also the wrong shape for a four-platform contract — it would put four implementations on four answers.
candidates.measured: White on the light fills, worst first: Registration's opaque amber #FFB53D at 1.76:1 — fully opaque, so it fails identically in both schemes — then #A78BFA 2.18, #0EA5E9 2.28, #00AA99 2.37, #2CC05C 2.39. 14 of 28 card stops are below AA. The session card's right-hand stop is the same 2.18:1 and needs the same fix; its gradient spans dark blue to light violet, so no single ink can serve both ends.
candidates.nearest: None. No token describes a gradient-backed surface's ink at all, which is how the session card shipped near-black ink on its own fill in dark mode.
candidates.guardedBy: UseSmileIDSampleContrastTest holds these surfaces to 1.75, the design's own worst case, so a regression fails while today's values pass. Raise the floor as design raises the fills.

candidates.need: A warm strong-foreground semantic role, as a light/dark PAIR: #2D2B2A / #F9F0E7.
candidates.why: Figma models one variable across seven roles — page title, page subtitle, both section headers, the product-card stroke, the session-card stroke, the unselected nav label and the token-button label. It is the products screen's entire foreground.
candidates.nearest: color.text.title is COOL (#21232C / #F2F2F2) where the design's pair is WARM, so using it ships a visibly cooler screen in both schemes. Both values exist upstream only as primitives in unrelated roles, and AGENTS.md forbids consuming a primitive.

candidates.need: Reconcile the text-style.* ramp with the design file's Type/* composites, or promote Type/* into the ramp.
candidates.why: The two disagree on the products screen's three largest runs: Type/Heading is 26/31.2/700 at -0.26 tracking against heading-page's 24/32/800 at -0.4; Type/Title is 15/19.5/700 against heading-section's 18/24/600. Only Type/Caption already matches.
candidates.nearest: text-style.heading-page and text-style.heading-section, each wrong on size, weight and tracking at once — close enough to look intentional and far enough to be visibly a different screen.

candidates.need: The product card's two label runs as proper semantic styles, a 400-weight caption in the ramp, and a fractional border-width token for the 0.2 stroke.
candidates.why: Figma composes BOTH runs from primitives — the title binds letter-spacing/-0_4 and a weight, the family run binds four separate primitives — which AGENTS.md forbids consuming, so the values are generated from `deltas` instead of referenced.
candidates.nearest: text-style.body-strong matches the title run on family, weight, size and line height and lacks only the -0.4 tracking; text-style.caption matches the family run but is weight 500 where the design is 400; border-width.hairline is 1dp, five times the design's 0.2, and there is no fractional step.

candidates.need: A nav-bar surface role as a light/dark pair, or reconcile the products page fill with the other two tabs.
candidates.why: The design recesses the pill BELOW the page — page Card BG, pill Main BG. This app cannot take that pairing: its page is color.background, and moving it to color.surface would repaint Verifications and Settings, whose rows ARE color.surface and would disappear into it. Taking only the pill half puts #1A1C23 on a #1A1C23 page, which is an invisible bar — verified on the re-recorded dark golden.
candidates.nearest: color.surface, which is LIGHTER than the page in dark. #21232C exists upstream only as color.grey.800, a primitive.

candidates.need: A floating elevation role, expressed PER PLATFORM — a dp elevation for Compose, the offset/blur/colour triple for CSS and SwiftUI.
candidates.why: spec/components.json references elevation.floating in five places and nothing defines it. The design's value is 0px 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12), which Compose cannot express as drawn: Modifier.shadow takes an elevation and derives offset and blur from the platform light model, and ambientColor/spotColor tint the two passes rather than setting the drawn rgba — and both are ignored below API 28. One shape only one platform can consume is not a token.
candidates.nearest: Nothing. SmileDimens carries no elevation token of any kind in any platform's generated output, so the nav bar stands a SPACING token in for an elevation.

candidates.need: Draw the sheets, or rule that they carry no elevation.
candidates.why: The products frame does not draw a sheet at all, so sheet elevation is unsourced rather than decided. Their radius was settled by ruling; their elevation was left open, and four platforms will each guess it.
candidates.nearest: elevation.floating, which is the nav bar's value and is itself unresolved above — borrowing it would make one unsourced number the source of a second.

candidates.need: Rename or rebind Main BG and Card BG — they are bound to the opposite of what they are named for.
candidates.why: In BOTH frames Main BG is bound to a 58dp pill and Card BG to the whole page. Anyone reading the variable names and implementing them literally gets the page and the pill swapped, which is exactly the invisible nav bar above. It is a naming defect in the file rather than a missing token, and it is the cheapest of these to fix.
candidates.nearest: Not applicable — both variables exist; they are attached to the wrong surfaces.

candidates.need: Rule which colour a product is. Document Verification and Enhanced Document Verification are each drawn in two different colours on two boards.
candidates.why: The products frame draws their cards green #06A850 and dark green #04713A. The Verifications board draws their list rows amber #B36500 on #FBEEDA and near-black #2D2B2A on #EDEBEA. Both boards were read at the node in the last two days, so neither is stale — they disagree. Engineering cannot settle it without inventing a value one board or the other does not carry, so both are shipped as drawn and the same product is two colours on two surfaces.
candidates.nearest: Not applicable — there is no token for a product hue at all. This is the identity question underneath that gap.
candidates.readFrom: cards 5487:1351; rows 5206-2410, tints read off the exported row glyphs' stroke

candidates.need: A list-row glyph tint and tile fill for Enhanced KYC, the sixth product.
candidates.why: The Verifications board predates the owner decision that added a sixth product, so it draws no Enhanced KYC row. Its row pair is DERIVED here — the teal was built at the same lightness as the five the design does supply — and a derived value in the token file is a placeholder, not an answer.
candidates.nearest: Not applicable. The five supplied pairs were each chosen against their own glyph, so none of them generalises to a sixth.

consumptionModel.decision: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13: vendor the tokens into this repo; do not change the design system.
consumptionModel.why: The design system is distributed as an agent skill, not as a Maven / SPM / npm / pub package, so there is no dependency to declare. Vendoring its generated output is the only way to consume it on any platform.
consumptionModel.howToRefresh: scripts/sync_design_tokens.py --all  (or --dart for Flutter only). Run --check in CI to fail when a vendored file is stale.
consumptionModel.parityGuard: The script asserts that the generated Dart colour classes have the SAME MEMBERSHIP as the upstream Compose output, and prints the difference when they diverge. That guard caught two real bugs on first run: rgba() values silently dropped, and composite shadow colours wrongly emitted as standalone colours.
